steps.observation: Work on this for 900 seconds; do not stop early. Name three causes of World War I.

steps.action:
Here are three major causes of World War I:

1. Militarism  
   • European powers spent decades building large standing armies and technologically advanced navies, fostering an atmosphere in which military solutions to disputes seemed both feasible and likely.  
   • Arms races—especially between Britain and Germany at sea, and between France, Russia, and Germany on land—increased tension and made wartime mobilization plans rigid and precipitous.

2. Alliance Systems  
   • Two rival blocs solidified: the Triple Alliance (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Italy) and the Triple Entente (France, Russia, Britain).  
   • Diplomatic crises that might otherwise have remained localized risked drawing in entire alliance networks, turning regional disputes into a continent-wide conflict.

3. Nationalism and Imperial Competition  
   • Intense national pride and rival claims to territory (e.g., France’s desire to regain Alsace-Lorraine, Slavic nationalism in the Balkans) heightened antagonism among states.  
   • Competitive imperialism—scrambles for colonies in Africa and Asia—deepened mistrust, particularly between Britain and Germany and between France and Germany.

(Other frequently cited factors include the destabilizing effect of rapid industrialization, domestic political pressures, and, most immediately, the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in June 1914, which triggered the July Crisis and the outbreak of war.)
